focus: OpenCode, Pi and Codex ask surfaces and turn-end blocking
noveltyJustification: Eight new findings: OpenCode's question tool and its observe-only event leg, Pi's two extension-provided ask tools and the absence of a blocking turn-end event, Codex's gated request_user_input, and the unproven Codex Stop block contract.
ruledOut: OpenCode event hook as a blocking channel
Codex PreToolUse as the enforcement point
Pi turn_end as a supported blocking event

label: OpenCode's built-in ask tool is named question; decision-capture reads part.tool === 'question' from real session storage.
No .opencode/agents definition sets a tools block or excludes question, so the repository does not gate OpenCode's ask tool by mode or flag.
OpenCode cannot block a turn end: tool.execute.before denies on throw, while event/session.idle is an observe-only subscription used by the advisory completion sentinel.
Pi has no built-in question tool; ask_user_question comes from @juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question and question from pi-plan-build, both enabled in .pi/settings.json.
Pi cannot block a turn end: agent_end has no result type, message_end can only replace the message, and only tool_call can return {block:true,reason}.
Codex's ask tool is request_user_input, gated by mode: Plan mode has it, Default mode only behind default_mode_request_user_input (enabled in .codex/config.toml), and codex exec never.
Codex request_user_input is auto-allowed and reaches PreToolUse while the operator decides, so PreToolUse is a positive ask signal but cannot detect a turn that never asks.
Codex Stop is wired but has no documented block contract here: only UserPromptSubmit exit 2 blocks, other non-zero exits fail open, and Stop stdout is parsed as a response envelope.

direction: OpenCode event hook as a blocking channel
reason: The event leg is a subscription with no return value; only tool.execute.before denies, by throwing.

direction: Codex PreToolUse as the enforcement point
reason: It fires only when a tool runs and cannot see a turn that ends with prose and no tool call.

direction: Pi turn_end as a supported blocking event
reason: ExtensionAPI declares no turn_end and agent_end has no result type, so the handler cannot block.
